Consult Summary:
- Forty-five-year-old woman with several months of painful, dry, cracked palmar skin with itching, likely dermatitis/contact dermatitis related to occupational exposure; management includes glove use, topical corticosteroid, and emollients with follow-up in 10–14 days or sooner if worse.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Soreness and cracking of skin on the hands, predominantly palms; dryness also noted on legs but less severe; itching present.
- Onset and progression: Symptoms began ~3–4 months ago; gradually worsened to the point of interfering with work; current pain significant.
- Exacerbating/initiating factors: Occupational exposure as a hotel housekeeper; inconsistent glove use; recently switched to a housekeeping role about 4 months ago; exposure to cleaning products suspected.
- Associated symptoms: Itching; scratching occasionally leads to bleeding; no spontaneous bleeding otherwise.
- Systems review: No fever, nausea, vomiting, abdominal/pelvic/bowel symptoms, or urinary symptoms reported; appetite preserved; general well-being otherwise.
- Relevant negatives: No reported skin problems previously; no systemic symptoms.
- Past Medical History: Diabetes mellitus type 2.
- Allergies: None reported.
- Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented); OTC emollient E45 used previously (dose/frequency not documented).
- Social History: Works as hotel housekeeper; exposure to cleaning products; glove use inconsistent; non-smoker; alcohol intake: couple of pints per week.
- Family History: Diabetes mellitus in the family; no known skin diseases reported.

Past Medical History:
- Diabetes mellitus type 2.
- Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented); OTC emollient E45 (dose/route/frequency not documented).

- Smoking: Never.

- Vitals: Not provided.

Investigations:
- Not performed or not documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Dermatitis / contact dermatitis suspected (palmar involvement, itch, cracking, occupational exposure).
  - Plan:
    - Avoid triggers: wear gloves during cleaning at all times.
    - Treatment: topical corticosteroid cream to reduce inflammation ( potency not specified in transcript ); prescribe and provide instructions to use as directed.
    - Moisturization: stronger emollients; apply to affected areas approximately 3–4 times daily for the next 2 weeks.
    - Follow-up: re-evaluate in about 10–14 days; if not improved or worsens (spread or increasing dryness), return sooner to consider additional options.
    - Education: discuss potential occupational trigger correlation; continue to avoid irritants where possible.
    - Access: prescription to be sent to the patient’s pharmacy.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies: documented as none in history; include explicit “no known drug allergies” in the note.
  - Vitals: not provided; consider recording if obtained later.
  - Med reconciliation: current medications listed (Metformin; OTC E45); consider confirming other OTC/topical products at follow-up.
  - Immunizations: not documented; consider noting if relevant for future visits.
- Internal conflicts: none detected between transcript statements.
- Transcript quality: Mostly clear; minor repetition and nonstandard phrasing; no critical omissions impacting the clinical plan.
